correctness.rationale: From the definition of the Petersen graph as disjoint pairs of two-subsets of a five-set, the included standalone checker exhausts all 32768 masks on its 15 graph edges. It verifies all 10869 nonempty faces, their exact f-vector, 5432 disjoint Morse cover pairs, 1 critical vertex and 4 critical 7-faces; a full topological sort of all 63780 Hasse cover incidences proves acyclicity. The resulting wedge of four 7-spheres is a proved premise. For each of the seven S5 cycle types, invariant faces are exactly unions of permitted graph-edge orbits; the signed augmented Lefschetz contribution for a union of k orbits is (-1)^(k+1). An independent fixed-face inversion-parity enumeration gives the same traces (4,2,0,1,-1,0,-1), equal to the five-point permutation trace minus 1. Rational representation character theory and invariant chains after barycentric subdivision prove the standard module and all subgroup quotient ranks. All quantifiers are on the fixed Petersen complex and on every subgroup of S5; no infinite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The exact published Petersen two-matching result establishes the nonequivariant wedge but does not determine the S5 rational character or the rational homology of all subgroup quotients. Direct searches for bounded-degree complexes, line-graph three-clique-free complexes, Kneser aliases, and equivariant Specht modules returned no equivalent or stronger indexed claim. Vega defines and computes other families, Singh treats complete and complete-bipartite families, and Ghosh–Selvaraja treats clique-free shellability rather than Petersen S5 representations. The new character cannot be inferred from the previously known four-dimensional Betti number. Residual risk: unindexed specialization or unpublished theorem.
residual_risks: The available databases and keyword searches cannot rule out an unindexed equivalent computation of the Petersen S5-module.
A broader equivariant bounded-degree-complex theorem not encountered could imply this special case, although none of the highly relevant inspected theorems does so.
Quotient integral torsion, integral S5-lattice structure, and generalization to other graphs are not settled.

value.rationale: For a canonical nonchordal cubic graph, the rational top homology was previously known only as a four-dimensional vector space. Identifying its entire natural S5 character with the standard five-letter module distinguishes inequivalent same-rank possibilities and produces a uniform all-subgroup quotient homology theorem: the seven-dimensional rational rank is precisely c(H)-1. This is a complete, naturally motivated equivariant invariant, not a routine Betti-count change or arbitrary parameter slice.
